changed_by.title: chore: bring the factory's files up to date

lesson.summary: The first implement run after pull request #586 did what the change claimed on the path it took: with one uncut session, "Save the session transcript" saved Fred's transcript as issue-627/20261122T181129Z-fred-run45052415270.json; nothing needs doing.
lesson.detail: Pull request #586 changed which execution file the implement workflow's "Save the session transcript" step passes to `save-session.sh`. The old step took the result of the last resume, falling back to an earlier one. The new step takes the file of the last session that began: when the time limit kills a session, that session's file is saved, not the earlier result again (decisions A418b). In run 45052415270, Fred's one session for issue #627 completed in 733 seconds for $0.89 over 22 turns. `continue-session.sh` printed "not continued: a pull request is ready for review for issue #627", so no resume ran. The step chose the first session's file and printed "saved fred session as issue-627/20261122T181129Z-fred-run45052415270.json", and that transcript is present. The run never cut a session short or resumed one, so the branch the change exists for is still proven only by the scripts' tests. Neither reviewer of pull request #586 recorded an assumption. I read the step's diff from Adam's review transcript, because `gh` and `git` needed approval in this session.

change.proposal: Nothing: the changed step did what pull request #586 claimed.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run succeeded, and its one session of 733 seconds and $0.89 opened the pull request it was started for.

lesson.saves: Nothing: there was no fault to prevent.
